\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ತೋರಣ} (tōraṇa)}{ತೋರಣ (tōraṇa)}]{\kn{ತೋರಣ} (tōraṇa) — a festoon of mango leaves (over a doorway)}

\label{lesson:KA-C262-torana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a lizard, then the Kannada for a cockroach.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ತೋರಣ}}
\textbf{\kn{ತೋರಣ}} — \emph{tōraṇa} — \textquotedblleft{}a festoon of mango leaves (over a doorway)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ತೋರಣ}} (\emph{tōraṇa}) is Sanskrit \emph{tōraṇa}, \textquotedblleft{}arched or festooned doorway\textquotedblright{}, taken over whole as a learned loan, a tatsama (CDIAL 5976).
\end{cousinweb}

\textbf{\kn{ಹೋಳಿಗೆ}} — \emph{hōḷige} — \textquotedblleft{}holige, a sweet stuffed flatbread\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಹೋಳಿಗೆ}} (\emph{hōḷige}) is probably a tadbhava of Sanskrit \emph{pōlī}, \textquotedblleft{}a cake of scorched grain and ghee\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8423), with \emph{p-} turned to \emph{h-} and an added \emph{-ige}; CDIAL does not list the Kannada word, but Marathi \emph{poḷī} is there.
\end{cousinweb}
